title: Capture ownership and shared, mutable, consuming invocation

environment.language: ISO C17; edition comparisons bounded by actually inspected sources
environment.target: Hosted Linux x86-64; exact-width integer types required
environment.dependencies: Original mechanisms from typed objects, loops and supplied allocation callbacks; host verification tools are separate. No mechanism-providing collection library.

passages: Call traits and coercions: FnOnce, FnMut, Fn and move capture note
layout.pointer.unsized: guarantees and non-guaranteed two-word observation
DESCRIPTION: mutex-associated predicate and atomic unlock/wait/relock
EXAMPLE: predicate loop under the same mutex
DESCRIPTION: ownership, default mutex and initialized-object requirements
RETURN VALUE, ERRORS and APPLICATION USAGE: normal versus robust mutexes

limitations: No exact published C17 text inspected.
Public executable anchors do not execute every written extension, independent measurement or delayed transfer.

rubric.criterion: Separate capture-by-value/reference from invocation capabilities and explain the documented Rust rule that move capture alone does not imply only FnOnce.
